```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 300,
  out.width = "100%",
  eval = requireNamespace("ggtree", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(scTreeSim)
library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
source("helpers.R")  # plotting helpers of the vignettes: plot_tree(), plot_binary(), ...
```

`sim_binary()` evolves binary sequences (e.g. presence/absence of mutations, or binarised
copy-number or methylation states) along a fixed tree. A simulation has three parts:

| part | what it does | arguments / functions |
|---|---|---|
| substitution model | how a site changes along a distance | `lambda`, `origin_seq` |
| clock model | how much distance each branch gets | `clock_strict()`, `clock_relaxed()`, `spike()` |
| tip error | what is observed at the tips | `alpha` (false negatives), `beta` (false positives) |

The clock turns branch lengths in time into **evolutionary distances**, in expected substitutions
per site. `clock_tree()` draws the distances and stores them in the tree, so that several simulations
can share one draw (`clock = NULL`), and `distance_tree()` returns the tree with the distances as branch lengths.
The output is a table of strings, one row per node, or a node x site table per sequence
(`write_as_string = FALSE`).

All simulations below use one sequence of 100 sites (`n_sites = 100`) on the multi-type tree of
`vignette("simulate_barcodes")`. The heatmaps show the sequences of the tips, one row per cell: a site
is 0 (white) or 1 (black).

```{r tree}
origin_time <- 3.6
ntype <- 2
shape <- c(100, 1)
scale <- 1 / shape
r <- 0.11
Xi_as <- matrix(c(0.0, 0.0, r, 0.0), nrow = ntype, ncol = ntype)
Xi_s  <- matrix(c(1 - r, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0), nrow = ntype, ncol = ntype)

set.seed(23)
tree <- sim_adb_origin_samp(origin_time, scale, shape, death_prob = c(0.1, 0.1),
                            sampling_prob = 0.8, origin_type = 0,
                            asym_trans_prob = Xi_as, sym_trans_prob = Xi_s, collapse = FALSE)
stopifnot(!is.null(tree))  # a simulation with too few tips returns NULL: try another seed

plot_tree(tree, color = "type", show_nodes = TRUE)
```

`collapse = FALSE` keeps the divisions and type changes of the tree as nodes. Divisions are needed
to place spikes (see below); the types to make them depend on the cell type.

# The substitution model

Each site evolves independently under a 2-state model: 0 -> 1 at rate 1 and 1 -> 0 at rate `lambda`,
scaled so that a distance of `d` gives `d` expected substitutions per site. A site in state 0 is in
state 1 after distance `d` with probability `pi1 * (1 - exp(-k * d))`, with equilibrium frequency
`pi1 = 1 / (1 + lambda)` of state 1 and `k = (1 + lambda)^2 / (2 * lambda)`:

```{r closed-form, fig.height = 3}
grid <- expand.grid(d = seq(0, 3, length.out = 200), lambda = c(0.25, 1, 4))
grid$p1 <- with(grid, 1 / (1 + lambda) * (1 - exp(-(1 + lambda)^2 / (2 * lambda) * d)))
grid$lambda <- factor(grid$lambda)
ggplot(grid, aes(d, p1, color = lambda)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 1 / (1 + as.numeric(as.character(lambda))), color = lambda),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(palette[1:3])) +
  labs(x = "distance d (expected substitutions per site)", y = "P(state 1 | state 0 at d = 0)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Sites saturate at their equilibrium (dashed) after a distance of about 1, so the distances of the
branches should mostly stay well below 1 to keep a phylogenetic signal.

Starting from a sequence of zeros at the origin (`origin_seq`) and a strict clock with 0.15
expected substitutions per site per unit of time:

```{r strict}
set.seed(1)
bin <- sim_binary(tree, n_sites = 100, origin_seq = rep(0L, 100), clock = clock_strict(0.15))
substr(head(bin, 3)$binary_1, 1, 40)  # the first 40 sites of the first three nodes
```

With `write_as_string = FALSE`, the same simulation is returned as a list with one node x site
table (integer 0/1) per sequence:

```{r strict-df}
set.seed(1)
bin_df <- sim_binary(tree, n_sites = 100, origin_seq = rep(0L, 100), clock = clock_strict(0.15),
                     write_as_string = FALSE)
bin_df$binary_1[1:3, 1:8]
```

```{r strict-plot}
plot_binary(tree, bin)
```

1s accumulate from the all-zero origin, and closely related cells share them. Without
`origin_seq`, the origin is drawn from the equilibrium, so `lambda` sets the frequency of 1s:

```{r lambda, fig.height = 8}
set.seed(5)
low <- sim_binary(tree, n_sites = 100, lambda = 0.25, clock = clock_strict(0.15))
high <- sim_binary(tree, n_sites = 100, lambda = 4, clock = clock_strict(0.15))
(plot_binary(tree, low) + labs(title = "lambda = 0.25")) /
  (plot_binary(tree, high) + labs(title = "lambda = 4")) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

# Clock models

A clock model gives every branch, including the root edge, a distance:

* `clock_strict(rate)`: `rate * length`, the same rate on all branches.
* `clock_relaxed(rate, dist, ...)`: `multiplier * rate * length`, with a multiplier of mean 1 drawn independently
  for every branch (`"lognormal"` with `sd`, `"gamma"` with `shape`, or `"exponential"`), as the
  uncorrelated relaxed clocks of BEAST2.
* `spike = spike(mean, shape, by_type)`, added to either clock: a burst of evolution at every cell division,
  added to the distances of both daughter branches.

## Strict and relaxed clocks

On a single-type tree, colouring the branches (in time) by their distance shows the difference:

```{r single-type, fig.height = 4.5}
set.seed(3)
tree1 <- sim_adb_origin_samp(4.5, scale = 0.25, shape = 4, death_prob = 0.1, sampling_prob = 0.6)

set.seed(1)
ct1_strict <- clock_tree(tree1, clock_strict(0.15))
ct1_relaxed <- clock_tree(tree1, clock_relaxed(0.15, sd = 1))
head(ct1_relaxed@data, 3)

lim <- c(0, max(ct1_strict@data$distance, ct1_relaxed@data$distance))  # one colour scale for both
(plot_tree(ct1_strict, color = "distance", limits = lim) + labs(title = "clock_strict(0.15)")) +
  (plot_tree(ct1_relaxed, color = "distance", limits = lim) + labs(title = "clock_relaxed(0.15, sd = 1)")) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

`clock_tree()` adds a `distance` column (one value per node, for the branch ending in it; the root's value
belongs to the root edge) and keeps the branch lengths in time. Under the strict clock the distance follows the
length of a branch; under the relaxed clock, branches of the same length evolve by very different
amounts.

## Spikes at divisions

`spike(mean)` adds `mean` expected substitutions per site to both daughter branches of every division
(`status == 2`). With `shape = Inf` (default) every spike is the same, which gives about
`Poisson(n_sites * mean)` substitutions per daughter branch; with a finite `shape` the spike is drawn
from a gamma distribution with this mean, and the counts are over-dispersed. `by_type` multiplies
`mean` by the type of the dividing cell.

We draw three clocks on the multi-type tree and store them, to plot the distances and simulate on the same draw:

```{r clocks}
set.seed(2)
ct_strict <- clock_tree(tree, clock_strict(0.15))
ct_relaxed <- clock_tree(tree, clock_relaxed(0.15, sd = 1))
ct_spike <- clock_tree(tree, clock_strict(0.05, spike = spike(0.05, shape = 2, by_type = c(1, 3))))
```

`plot_distance_tree()` draws the distance tree (`distance_tree()`):

```{r distance-trees, fig.height = 8}
(plot_tree(tree, color = "type") + labs(title = "time")) +
  (plot_distance_tree(ct_strict) + labs(title = "strict")) +
  (plot_distance_tree(ct_relaxed) + labs(title = "relaxed")) +
  (plot_distance_tree(ct_spike) + labs(title = "strict + spikes")) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2, guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The strict distance tree is the time tree, rescaled. The relaxed clock stretches and shrinks single
branches. With spikes, every branch that starts at a division is longer, most of all after divisions of
type 1 cells (three times the spike).

`clock = NULL` simulates on the stored distances, so the sequences belong to the distance trees above:

```{r relaxed-plot}
set.seed(3)
bin_relaxed <- sim_binary(ct_relaxed, n_sites = 100, clock = NULL)
plot_binary(ct_relaxed, bin_relaxed, distance = TRUE)
```

Next to the distance tree, the differences between sequences follow the distances, not the time:
the cells at the top, separated by short distances, have almost the same sequence, whereas the two
cells at the end of the long type 0 branch (bottom) differ more from all other cells than most pairs do.

```{r spike-plot}
set.seed(3)
bin_spike <- sim_binary(ct_spike, n_sites = 100, clock = NULL)
plot_binary(ct_spike, bin_spike)
```

With spikes, the type 1 cells, whose divisions add the most distance, are more diverse than the
type 0 cells, although both have evolved for the same time.

The spike shape sets how variable the substitutions per division are. Here, with spikes only
(`rate = 0`) of mean 0.05 at all divisions, we count the sites that differ between a daughter cell
and its parent (`write_as_string = FALSE`), over 30 simulations:

```{r spike-counts, fig.height = 3}
# branches that start at a division
tree_df <- tibble::as_tibble(tree)
div_edges <- tree_df[tree_df$parent != tree_df$node & tree_df$parent %in% tree_df$node[tree_df$status == 2], ]

count_substitutions <- function(shape, n_rep = 30) {
  clk <- clock_strict(0, spike = spike(0.05, shape = shape))
  unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_rep), function(i) {
    s <- as.matrix(sim_binary(tree, n_sites = 100, clock = clk, write_as_string = FALSE)$binary_1[-1])
    rowSums(s[div_edges$node, ] != s[div_edges$parent, ])
  }))
}
set.seed(6)
counts <- rbind(data.frame(spike = "fixed (shape = Inf)", n = count_substitutions(Inf)),
                data.frame(spike = "gamma (shape = 1)", n = count_substitutions(1)))
aggregate(n ~ spike, counts, function(x) round(c(mean = mean(x), var = var(x)), 1))

pois <- expand.grid(n = 0:25, spike = unique(counts$spike))
pois$p <- dpois(pois$n, 5)
ggplot(counts, aes(n)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y = after_stat(prop)), fill = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = pois, aes(n, p), color = palette[[4]], size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ spike) +
  labs(x = "substitutions on a daughter branch", y = "proportion") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Fixed spikes give about Poisson(5) counts (points); the mean is slightly below 5 because a few sites
change back. Gamma spikes with `shape = 1` have the same mean but a variance of about
`5 + 5^2 / shape`.

Spikes are only placed at divisions that are nodes of the tree. A collapsed tree (`collapse = TRUE`) hides
divisions on its branches; their number can be given in a `hidden_divisions` column of the tree data
(see `?spike`).

# Error at the tips

`alpha` and `beta` are the probabilities of observing a 0 for a true 1 (false negative) and a 1 for a true 0
(false positive). They act at the tips only, after evolution, so the internal nodes keep their true
states and errors are not inherited. Error is drawn after the sequences, so with the same seed the true
sequences are the same with and without error:

```{r error}
set.seed(4)
true <- sim_binary(ct_strict, n_sites = 100, clock = NULL)
set.seed(4)
observed <- sim_binary(ct_strict, n_sites = 100, clock = NULL, alpha = 0.1, beta = 0.05)
plot_binary(ct_strict, observed, errors = true, color = "none")
```

The marked sites were flipped by the error: about 10% of the 1s and 5% of the 0s. Unlike
substitutions, errors are not shared by relatives.

# Other substitution models

`distance_tree()` makes the clock models usable with other simulators, e.g. `phangorn::simSeq()` for
other substitution models. The same 2-state model in phangorn, which also scales its rate matrix to
one expected substitution per unit of branch length:

```{r phangorn, eval = requireNamespace("phangorn", quietly = TRUE)}
lambda <- 1
set.seed(7)
seqs <- phangorn::simSeq(distance_tree(ct_relaxed)@phylo, l = 100, Q = 1,
                         bf = c(lambda, 1) / (lambda + 1), type = "USER", levels = c("0", "1"))
substr(unname(apply(as.character(seqs), 1, paste, collapse = ""))[1:3], 1, 40)
```

phangorn starts from the equilibrium at the root and ignores the root edge.

# Choosing a clock

* **Strict** (`clock_strict()`): all lineages evolve at the same rate, e.g. a constant mutation rate per time.
* **Relaxed** (`clock_relaxed()`): rates vary between branches, e.g. lineages with different mutation rates;
  `sd` (lognormal) or `shape` (gamma) set how much.
* **Spikes** (`spike()`): mutations arise at cell divisions, e.g. replication errors or chromosomal changes
  at mitosis; `shape` sets how variable they are, `by_type` makes them depend on the cell type.
  Spikes add to a strict or relaxed clock, or replace it (`rate = 0`).
